answer: A protocol requires agents to lock bonded compute collateral within a verifiable execution lattice, where each identity blooms like a lotus in an epoch registry. Rather than relying on an ivory tower of centralized trust, nodes challenge peers to re-execute cryptographic puzzles tied to deterministic states. An adversary attempting to forge multiple identity certificates faces superlinear hardware and token-slashing costs, making mass clone deployment economically unviable as capital requirements exceed potential extraction.
